question: After the sanitizer and shrinkwrap blockers are fixed, should OpenClaw accept the bounded `gateway_restart_audit` shared-state table with redacted source/session/preflight metadata?
rationale: Automation can repair the concrete redaction and lockfile defects, but deciding what restart preflight/audit metadata may be durably stored is a privacy and security-boundary choice.

options.title: Accept after blockers are fixed
options.body: Keep the bounded shared-SQLite restart-audit table after sensitive parent objects are redacted and the dependency graph is clean.

options.title: Narrow stored metadata
options.body: Keep the table but remove or further summarize preflight/context fields before merge to reduce durable privacy exposure.

options.title: Pause durable storage
options.body: Pause or close this PR if restart attribution should stay in logs or wait for a broader audit-ledger design.

recommendation.title: Accept after blockers are fixed
recommendation.body: Keep the bounded shared-SQLite restart-audit table after sensitive parent objects are redacted and the dependency graph is clean.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent audit-design and shared-state history make them the best available owner for the persistent audit privacy boundary decision.
